phase1.explanation:
🦀 **Generics let you write code that works with many types.**

**Generic syntax:**

| Feature | Syntax |
|---------|--------|
| Function | `fn f<T>(x: T) -> T` |
| Struct | `struct S<T> { field: T }` |
| Enum | `enum E<T> { Variant(T) }` |
| Method | `impl<T> S<T> { fn method(&self) -> &T }` |

**Rust-chan says:**
"Generics are for when you want code to work with multiple types without duplication."

**When to use generics:**
| Situation | Use generics |
|-----------|--------------|
| Multiple types with same behavior | ✅ |
| Reusable code | ✅ |
| Collections | ✅ |
| Algorithms | ✅ |
phase1.openingDialogue: Generics. Write once, use with many types. 🦀
